कारण (R) : अधिकांश प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले ऐमीनो अम्लों में L-विन्यास होता है ।

Assertion (A) : All naturally occurring α-amino acids except glycine are optically active.
Reason (R) : Most naturally occurring amino acids have L-configuration.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर चुनकर दीजिए।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). Glycine (H2N-CH2-COOH) has no chiral carbon because both substituents on the alpha carbon are hydrogen atoms, so it is optically inactive. All other naturally occurring alpha-amino acids have a chiral alpha carbon, making them optically active — hence Assertion (A) is correct. Reason (R) is also independently true: most naturally occurring amino acids do indeed have the L-configuration. However, the L-configuration is not the cause of optical activity; optical activity arises from the presence of a chiral centre, not from which configuration (L or D) the molecule adopts. Therefore Reason (R) does not correctly explain Assertion (A), making option (B) the correct choice.

options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: ethanol (boiling point 78.4°C) has a significantly higher boiling point than methoxymethane (dimethyl ether, boiling point −24°C). This is because ethanol molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other through their O-H groups, requiring more energy to separate, whereas methoxymethane has no O-H bond and cannot form hydrogen bonds. However, Reason (R) is false: ethanol does NOT have intramolecular hydrogen bonding. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding occurs within a single molecule (as in o-nitrophenol), but ethanol is too small and its O-H group cannot form a hydrogen bond within the same molecule. The correct type of hydrogen bonding in ethanol is intermolecular. Therefore option (C) is correct.

Assertion (A) : The boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order : RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Reason (R) : The boiling points of alkyl chlorides, bromides and iodides are considerably higher than that of the hydrocarbon of comparable molecular mass.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

questions.solution: Both statements are true, but Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). Assertion (A) is correct: the boiling points of alkyl halides with the same alkyl group decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF because boiling point increases with increasing molecular mass and larger, more polarisable halogens increase London dispersion forces. Reason (R) is also independently true: alkyl chlorides, bromides and iodides have higher boiling points than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass due to the greater polarity and higher molecular mass contributed by the halogen. However, Reason (R) explains why alkyl halides boil higher than hydrocarbons, not why the order among halides is RI > RBr > RCl > RF. Since both are true but R does not explain A, option (B) is correct.

Assertion (A) : [Cr(H2O)6]Cl2 and [Fe(H2O)6]Cl2 are examples of homoleptic complexes.
Reason (R) : All the ligands attached to the metal are the same.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). A homoleptic complex is one in which the metal is bonded to only one type of donor group (ligand). In [Cr(H2O)6]Cl2 and [Fe(H2O)6]Cl2, the coordination sphere (the part inside the square brackets) contains only water (H2O) ligands bonded to the central metal ion; the Cl- ions are counter ions outside the coordination sphere. Since all ligands within the complex are identical water molecules, both complexes are correctly classified as homoleptic. Reason (R) — that all ligands attached to the metal are the same — is the exact definition of a homoleptic complex and thus correctly explains Assertion (A). Option (A) is correct.

questions.text: अचार बनाने के लिए नमक के सांद्र विलयन में रखा गया कच्चा आम सिकुड़ जाता है, क्योंकि _______
questions.text_english: An unripe mango placed in a concentrated salt solution to prepare pickle, shrivels because _______.

options.A: यह परासरण के कारण जल प्राप्त करता है ।
options.B: यह उत्क्रम परासरण के कारण जल खो देता है ।
options.C: यह उत्क्रम परासरण के कारण जल प्राप्त करता है ।
options.D: यह परासरण के कारण जल खो देता है ।

options_english.A: it gains water due to osmosis
options_english.B: it loses water due to reverse osmosis
options_english.C: it gains water due to reverse osmosis
options_english.D: it loses water due to osmosis

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): the mango loses water due to osmosis. The concentrated salt solution outside the mango has a much higher solute concentration (lower water potential) than the cell sap inside the mango. In osmosis, water moves from a region of higher water concentration (lower solute concentration) to a region of lower water concentration (higher solute concentration) through a semi-permeable membrane. Therefore, water flows out of the mango cells into the concentrated salt solution, causing the cells to lose turgor and the mango to shrivel. This is simple osmosis, not reverse osmosis; reverse osmosis requires an externally applied pressure greater than osmotic pressure to force water against the concentration gradient.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन ग्लूकोज़ के विषय में सत्य नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements is not true about glucose ?

options.B: HI के साथ गर्म करने पर यह n-हेक्सेन बनाता है ।
options.C: यह फ्यूरेनोस रूप में उपस्थित होता है ।

options_english.B: On heating with HI it forms n-hexane.
options_english.D: It does not give Schiff's test.

questions.solution: The statement that is NOT true about glucose is option (C): glucose does not exist in the furanose form. Glucose is a six-carbon aldosugar (aldohexose) — option (A) is true. When heated with HI (hydroiodic acid), glucose undergoes reduction of all its hydroxyl groups to give n-hexane — option (B) is true. Glucose does not give Schiff's test even though it contains an aldehyde group, because the open-chain form is present in very small proportion in solution (most exists in the cyclic hemiacetal pyranose form) — option (D) is true. Glucose undergoes intramolecular hemiacetal formation between the C-1 aldehyde and the C-5 hydroxyl to form a six-membered pyranose ring, not a five-membered furanose ring. Furanose is formed from C-4 hydroxy groups, which is characteristic of fructose. Hence option (C) is the correct answer.

questions.text: प्रोपेनेमाइड को प्रोपेनेमीन में परिवर्तित करने के लिए सबसे उत्तम अभिकर्मक _________ है ।
questions.text_english: The best reagent for converting propanamide into propanamine is _______.

options.C: लाल फॉस्फोरस की उपस्थिति में आयोडीन

options_english.C: iodine in the presence of red phosphorus

questions.solution: The best reagent for converting propanamide (CH3CH2CONH2) into propanamine (CH3CH2CH2NH2) is (D) LiAlH4 in ether. LiAlH4 is a powerful reducing agent that reduces amides to amines by providing hydride ions. The reaction reduces the C=O of the amide while retaining the C-N bond, giving a primary amine with the same carbon chain. Option (A) excess H2 is not effective for reducing amides under normal conditions. Option (B) Br2/NaOH is the Hofmann bromamide reaction which converts amides to amines with one carbon less (propanamide would give ethanamine, CH3CH2NH2), so it is not the correct transformation here. Option (C) I2/red phosphorus is used for the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction on carboxylic acids. Therefore, LiAlH4 in ether is the correct and best reagent.
questions.topic: Preparation of Amines — Reduction of Amides

questions.text: प्रोपिल मैग्नीशियम ब्रोमाइड को CO2 के साथ अभिक्रियत करने के पश्चात् अम्ल जलअपघटन करने पर बनने वाला अम्ल है
questions.text_english: The acid formed when propyl magnesium bromide is treated with CO2 followed by acid hydrolysis is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) C3H7COOH (butanoic acid). When a Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 (dry ice), it undergoes a nucleophilic addition reaction: the carbanion of the Grignard reagent attacks the carbon of CO2 to form a magnesium salt of a carboxylic acid. On subsequent acid hydrolysis with dilute mineral acid, the salt gives the free carboxylic acid. Propyl magnesium bromide (C3H7MgBr) reacts with CO2 to form C3H7COOMgBr, and on acid hydrolysis this gives C3H7COOH, which is butanoic acid. The carbon chain increases by one carbon unit (from 3 to 4), because CO2 contributes the carboxyl group. Options (B) and (C) are shorter chain acids and would arise from a shorter Grignard reagent. Option (D) is an alcohol, not an acid.
questions.topic: Preparation of Carboxylic Acids — Grignard Reaction

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में अम्ल सामर्थ्य का सही क्रम कौन सा है ?
questions.text_english: Which is the correct order of acid strength from the following ?
questions.solution: The correct order of acid strength is (A): C6H5OH > H2O > ROH. Phenol (C6H5OH) is the strongest acid among the three because after losing a proton, the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance — the negative charge is delocalised over the benzene ring, making phenol more willing to donate a proton (pKa ≈ 10). Water (H2O) is a stronger acid than alcohols because the oxygen in water is bonded to hydrogen only, and its conjugate base (OH-) is more stable than an alkoxide ion. Alcohols (ROH) are the weakest acids because the alkyl group (+I effect) increases electron density on oxygen, making it less willing to release a proton, and the alkoxide ion (RO-) is less stable. Hence the decreasing order of acidity is: phenol > water > alcohol.
questions.topic: Acidic Nature of Phenols and Alcohols

questions.text: नाभिकरागी द्विआणविक प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया से गुजरने वाले ऐल्किल हैलाइड में सम्मिलित है
questions.text_english: Alkyl halides undergoing nucleophilic bimolecular substitution reaction involve
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) inversion of configuration. In an SN2 (nucleophilic bimolecular substitution) reaction, the nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon from the back side — i.e., from the side opposite to the leaving group. This back-side attack results in a Walden inversion (umbrella-like inversion of the tetrahedral configuration), similar to an umbrella turning inside out. If the substrate is optically active, the product has the opposite configuration. Option (A) retention is characteristic of SN1 reactions with neighbouring group participation. Option (B) racemic mixture formation occurs in SN1 reactions where a planar carbocation intermediate is formed. Option (D) carbocation formation is also a feature of SN1 reactions, not SN2.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांक के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें : (i) (CH3)2CH-CH2Br, (ii) CH3CH2CH2CH2Br, (iii) (CH3)3C-Br । सही क्रम है
questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling points : (i) (CH3)2CH-CH2Br, (ii) CH3CH2CH2CH2Br, (iii) (CH3)3C-Br. The correct order is
questions.solution: The correct order is (C): (iii) < (i) < (ii). All three compounds have the same molecular formula C4H9Br (same molecular mass), so the difference in boiling points is determined by branching. More branching leads to a more compact, spherical shape, which reduces the surface area available for intermolecular van der Waals interactions, thereby lowering the boiling point. Compound (iii), (CH3)3C-Br (2-bromo-2-methylpropane, tertiary), is the most branched and has the lowest boiling point (~73°C). Compound (i), (CH3)2CH-CH2Br (1-bromo-2-methylpropane, primary but branched), is less branched than (iii) but more branched than (ii), so it has an intermediate boiling point (~91°C). Compound (ii), CH3CH2CH2CH2Br (1-bromobutane), is a straight-chain primary alkyl bromide with the maximum surface area and thus the highest boiling point (~102°C).
questions.topic: Effect of Branching on Boiling Points

questions.text: [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]2+ का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]2+ is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Diamminedichloridoplatinum (IV). To find the oxidation state of Pt: the complex ion [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]2+ carries an overall charge of +2. NH3 is a neutral ligand (charge = 0) and Cl- carries a charge of -1 each. Let the oxidation state of Pt = x. Then x + 2(0) + 2(-1) = +2, giving x - 2 = +2, so x = +4. The oxidation state of platinum is +4. The IUPAC name lists ligands alphabetically: ammine (NH3) before chlorido (Cl-), with their prefixes di- each. Since the complex is cationic, the metal is named as 'platinum' (not 'platinate'). Option (D) uses 'platinate' which is used for anionic complexes. Options (A) and (C) give incorrect oxidation states (+2 and 0 respectively).

questions.text: अम्लीय KMnO4 सल्फाइट को ऑक्सीकृत कर देता है
questions.text_english: Acidified KMnO4 oxidises sulphite to
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) SO4^2- (sulphate). Acidified KMnO4 is a strong oxidising agent. When sulphite ions (SO3^2-, sulphur in +4 oxidation state) are oxidised by acidified KMnO4, the sulphur is oxidised from +4 to +6, producing sulphate ions (SO4^2-). The reaction is: 5SO3^2- + 2MnO4- + 6H+ → 5SO4^2- + 2Mn^2+ + 3H2O. The permanganate is reduced from +7 (MnO4-) to +2 (Mn^2+, colourless solution) while sulphite is oxidised to sulphate. Option (A) thiosulphate would require a different reaction condition. Option (B) peroxodisulphate is a very strong oxidiser itself and would not be a product. Option (C) SO2 would be a reduction product, not an oxidation product.

questions.text: चुंबकीय आघूर्ण इसके प्रचक्रणी कोणीय संवेग और कक्षीय कोणीय संवेग से जुड़ा होता है । Cr3+ आयन (परमाणु क्रमांक : Cr = 24) का प्रचक्रण मात्र चुंबकीय आघूर्ण मान _________ है ।
questions.text_english: The magnetic moment is associated with its spin angular momentum and orbital angular momentum. Spin only magnetic moment value of Cr3+ ion (Atomic no. : Cr = 24) is _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 3.87 B.M. Chromium (Cr) has atomic number 24. Its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d5 4s1. In Cr3+, three electrons are removed to give [Ar] 3d3. The 3d3 configuration has 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only magnetic moment formula is: μ = √(n(n+2)) B.M., where n = number of unpaired electrons. Substituting n = 3: μ = √(3 × 5) = √15 ≈ 3.87 B.M. For reference: n=1 gives 1.73 B.M., n=2 gives 2.83 B.M., n=3 gives 3.87 B.M., n=4 gives 4.90 B.M. Therefore, the spin-only magnetic moment of Cr3+ is 3.87 B.M.
questions.topic: Magnetic Properties of Transition Metal Ions

questions.text: Sn4+/Sn2+ युग्म के लिए मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव +0.15 V और Cr3+/Cr युग्म के लिए यह −0.74 V है । दो युग्म अपनी मानक अवस्थाओं में संयोजित होकर एक सेल का निर्माण करते हैं । सेल विभव होगा
questions.text_english: Standard electrode potential for Sn4+/Sn2+ couple is +0.15 V and that for the Cr3+/Cr couple is −0.74 V. The two couples in their standard states are connected to make a cell. The cell potential will be
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) +0.89 V. In a galvanic cell, the electrode with the higher (more positive) reduction potential acts as the cathode (where reduction occurs) and the one with the lower (more negative) reduction potential acts as the anode (where oxidation occurs). Here, E°(Sn4+/Sn2+) = +0.15 V and E°(Cr3+/Cr) = −0.74 V. The Sn4+/Sn2+ couple has the higher reduction potential, so Sn4+ is reduced at the cathode. The Cr3+/Cr couple has the lower reduction potential, so Cr is oxidised at the anode (Cr → Cr3+ + 3e-). Cell potential E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = +0.15 − (−0.74) = +0.15 + 0.74 = +0.89 V.
questions.topic: Cell Potential and Standard Electrode Potential

questions.text: संगुणन में विलेय का अपसामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान
questions.text_english: In case of association, abnormal molar mass of solute will
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): in the case of association, the abnormal molar mass of the solute will increase. Association means that solute molecules come together to form larger aggregates (dimers, trimers, etc.) in solution — for example, acetic acid forms dimers in benzene due to hydrogen bonding. This reduces the actual number of solute particles in solution compared to what would be expected if no association occurred. Colligative properties (like elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure) depend on the number of solute particles. Fewer particles mean smaller colligative property values. When the molar mass is calculated using colligative property equations, a smaller observed effect (due to fewer particles) gives a larger calculated molar mass. Hence, the experimentally determined (abnormal) molar mass is greater than the true molar mass in association.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक अनुक्रम अभिक्रिया में A और B की पहचान कीजिए :
(a) CH3CH2Cl → (NaCN) → A → (H2/Ni) → B
(b) C6H5NH2 → (NaNO2/HCl, 0-5°C) → A → (C6H5NH2/H+) → B
questions.text_english:
Identify A and B in each of the following reaction sequence :
(a) CH3CH2Cl → (NaCN) → A → (H2/Ni) → B
(b) C6H5NH2 → (NaNO2/HCl, 0-5°C) → A → (C6H5NH2/H+) → B

key_points: (a) A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile/propanenitrile); B = CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propylamine/propan-1-amine)
(b) A = C6H5N2+Cl- (benzene diazonium chloride); B = C6H5-NH-N=N-C6H5 (diazoaminobenzene / N-(phenylazo)aniline)

questions.solution:
(a) CH3CH2Cl (chloroethane) reacts with NaCN via SN2 reaction to give CH3CH2CN (propanenitrile) as compound A. The cyanide ion acts as a nucleophile and replaces the chloride, extending the carbon chain by one carbon. Compound A (CH3CH2CN) then undergoes catalytic reduction with H2/Ni to give CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propan-1-amine) as compound B, since reduction of a nitrile gives a primary amine.

(b) Aniline (C6H5NH2) reacts with NaNO2 and HCl at 0-5°C in the Diazotisation reaction to form C6H5N2+Cl- (benzenediazonium chloride) as compound A. This diazonium salt then reacts with aniline (C6H5NH2) in the presence of H+ in a coupling-type reaction to give C6H5-NH-N=N-C6H5 (diazoaminobenzene, also called N-phenylazo-aniline) as compound B.

questions.text_english: When FeCr2O4 is fused with Na2CO3 in the presence of air it gives a yellow solution of compound (A). Compound (A) on acidification gives compound (B). Compound (B) on reaction with KCl forms an orange coloured (C). An acidified solution of compound (C) oxidises iodide to (D). Identify (A), (B), (C) and (D).

key_points: A = Na2CrO4 (sodium chromate, yellow)
B = Na2Cr2O7 (sodium dichromate, orange)
C = K2Cr2O7 (potassium dichromate, orange)
D = I2 (iodine)

questions.solution: When FeCr2O4 (chromite ore) is fused with Na2CO3 in the presence of air, chromium is oxidised from Cr3+ to Cr6+, forming sodium chromate Na2CrO4 (compound A), which gives a yellow solution. On acidification, the chromate ion (CrO4^2-) undergoes disproportionation in acidic medium: 2CrO4^2- + 2H+ → Cr2O7^2- + H2O, giving sodium dichromate Na2Cr2O7 (compound B). Compound B reacts with KCl to give potassium dichromate K2Cr2O7 (compound C), which is orange coloured. Acidified K2Cr2O7 is a strong oxidising agent; it oxidises iodide ions (I-) to iodine I2 (compound D): Cr2O7^2- + 6I- + 14H+ → 2Cr3+ + 3I2 + 7H2O.

questions.text_english: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal ? Justify your answer.

key_points: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition reactions.

In benzaldehyde, the carbonyl carbon is conjugated with the benzene ring; the lone pair of the ring delocalises into the C=O group, reducing the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon and making it less electrophilic.
In propanal, the ethyl group has a weak +I effect, but there is no conjugation, so the carbonyl carbon remains more electrophilic and more susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

questions.solution: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal towards nucleophilic addition reactions. In benzaldehyde, the carbonyl group (C=O) is directly conjugated with the aromatic benzene ring. This conjugation allows the pi electrons of the ring to delocalise into the carbonyl group, reducing the partial positive charge (delta+) on the carbonyl carbon and making it less susceptible to attack by a nucleophile. In contrast, propanal has a simple alkyl group attached to the carbonyl carbon; the alkyl group exerts a weak positive inductive effect (+I) but there is no resonance deactivation of the carbonyl. Therefore, the carbonyl carbon in propanal remains more electrophilic and reacts more readily with nucleophiles.

questions.text_english:
(A) Give reasons : (a) Cooking is faster in pressure cooker than in an open pan. (b) On mixing liquid X and liquid Y, volume of the resulting solution decreases. What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by the resulting solution ? What change in temperature would you observe after mixing liquids X and Y ?
OR
(B) Define Azeotrope. What type of Azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult's law ? Give an example.

key_points: (A)(a) In a pressure cooker, pressure is higher than atmospheric pressure, which raises the boiling point of water, so cooking occurs at a higher temperature and is faster.

(A)(b) Decrease in volume on mixing indicates stronger intermolecular interactions between X and Y than between X-X or Y-Y. This shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. The temperature of the solution increases (exothermic mixing).

(B) Azeotrope: a mixture of two liquids that boils at a constant temperature and has the same composition in liquid and vapour phases. Negative deviation forms a maximum boiling azeotrope. Example: HNO3 + H2O (68% HNO3, boiling point 393.5 K).

questions.solution:
(A)(a) In a pressure cooker, the vapour cannot escape and pressure builds up above atmospheric pressure. According to the relationship between boiling point and pressure, an increase in pressure raises the boiling point of water. Water therefore boils at a temperature higher than 100°C inside the cooker, so food cooks faster.

(A)(b) When mixing X and Y causes the volume to decrease, it means the molecules of X and Y interact more strongly with each other than they do with molecules of the same type. This leads to a negative deviation from Raoult's law (observed vapour pressure is lower than expected). The stronger interactions release energy, so the mixing process is exothermic and the temperature of the solution increases after mixing.

OR

(B) An azeotrope (constant boiling mixture) is a binary mixture that has the same composition in the liquid and vapour phases at a given temperature and pressure, and therefore distils without change in composition. A negative deviation from Raoult's law (stronger A-B interactions) leads to a maximum boiling azeotrope, where the boiling point of the mixture is higher than that of either pure component. Example: nitric acid and water mixture (68% HNO3 by mass) forms a maximum boiling azeotrope boiling at 393.5 K.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के कारण दीजिए : (a) ऐमीनो अम्लों के गलनांक सामान्यतः संगत कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों की तुलना में अधिक होते हैं । (b) ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी व्यवहार दर्शाते हैं ।
questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following : (a) The melting points of α-amino acids are generally higher than that of the corresponding carboxylic acids. (b) Amino acids show amphoteric behaviour.

key_points: (a) Amino acids exist as zwitterions (dipolar ions) in the solid state, with strong ionic interactions holding the lattice together, which require more energy to break — hence higher melting points than the corresponding carboxylic acids.
(b) Amino acids have both an acidic carboxyl group (-COOH) and a basic amino group (-NH2). They can donate a proton (act as an acid) or accept a proton (act as a base), showing amphoteric behaviour.

questions.solution:
(a) Amino acids exist in the solid state as zwitterions (also called dipolar ions), where the amino group (-NH2) accepts a proton from the carboxyl group (-COOH) to form -NH3+ and -COO- within the same molecule. These charged groups create strong electrostatic (ionic) interactions between neighbouring zwitterion molecules in the crystal lattice, similar to ionic compounds. Breaking these ionic interactions requires considerably more energy than breaking the weaker van der Waals and hydrogen bonding forces present in carboxylic acids, which do not form zwitterions. Hence amino acids have higher melting points than corresponding carboxylic acids.

(b) Amino acids contain both an acidic group (-COOH, which can donate H+) and a basic group (-NH2, which can accept H+). In acidic solution, the -NH2 group accepts a proton to become -NH3+, making the molecule a cation. In basic solution, the -COOH group donates a proton to become -COO-, making the molecule an anion. Because they can behave both as an acid and as a base depending on the pH, amino acids are said to be amphoteric.
questions.topic: Properties of Amino Acids — Zwitterion and Amphoteric Nature

questions.text: जल में प्रति लीटर 15 ग्राम यूरिया (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 60 g mol−1) वाले विलयन का परासरण दाब जल में ग्लूकोज़ (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol−1) के विलयन के समान (समपरासरी) है । इसके एक लीटर विलयन में उपस्थित ग्लूकोज़ का द्रव्यमान परिकलित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A solution containing 15 g urea (molar mass = 60 g mol−1) per litre of solution in water has the same osmotic pressure (isotonic) as a solution of glucose (molar mass = 180 g mol−1) in water. Calculate the mass of glucose present in one litre of its solution.

key_points: Molarity of urea = 15/60 = 0.25 mol/L
For isotonic solutions, molarities are equal, so molarity of glucose = 0.25 mol/L
Mass of glucose = 0.25 × 180 = 45 g

questions.solution:
Two solutions are isotonic when they have the same osmotic pressure (π = CRT). Since both solutions are at the same temperature (T) and R is a constant, isotonic solutions must have equal molar concentrations (C).

Molarity of urea solution = mass / (molar mass × volume in litres) = 15 / (60 × 1) = 0.25 mol L−1.

Since the glucose solution is isotonic with the urea solution, its molarity is also 0.25 mol L−1.

Mass of glucose = Molarity × Molar mass × Volume = 0.25 × 180 × 1 = 45 g.

Therefore, the mass of glucose present in one litre of its solution is 45 g.

अभिक्रिया के लिए Δr G° और log KC परिकलित कीजिए :
Fe2+(aq) + Ag+(aq) → Fe3+(aq) + Ag(s)
दिया गया है : E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Fe3+/Fe2+ = 0.77 V
[R = 8.314 J K−1 mol−1, F = 96500 C mol−1]
questions.text_english:
Calculate Δr G° and log KC of the reaction :
Fe2+(aq) + Ag+(aq) → Fe3+(aq) + Ag(s)
Given E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Fe3+/Fe2+ = 0.77 V
[R = 8.314 J K−1 mol−1, F = 96500 C mol−1]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.80 - 0.77 = 0.03 V

questions.solution:
In the given reaction, Ag+ is reduced to Ag (cathode: Ag+ + e- → Ag, E° = +0.80 V) and Fe2+ is oxidised to Fe3+ (anode: Fe2+ → Fe3+ + e-, E° = +0.77 V). Number of electrons transferred, n = 1.

E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − 0.77 = +0.03 V.

Δr G° = −nFE°cell = −1 × 96500 × 0.03 = −2895 J mol−1 = −2.895 kJ mol−1.

Using the relation Δr G° = −2.303 RT log KC:
−2895 = −2.303 × 8.314 × 298 × log KC
log KC = 2895 / (2.303 × 8.314 × 298) = 2895 / 5706.5 ≈ 0.507.

Alternatively, log KC = nE°cell / 0.0591 = (1 × 0.03) / 0.0591 ≈ 0.507.

(a) निम्नलिखित को pKb के घटते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : ऐनिलीन, p-नाइट्रोऐनिलीन, p-मेथिलऐनिलीन
(b) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (i) ऐलीफैटिक ऐमीनों की तुलना में ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीनों के डाइज़ोनियम लवण अधिक स्थायी होते हैं । (ii) जल में मेथिलऐमीन, FeCl3 के साथ अभिक्रिया करके जलयोजित फेरिक ऑक्साइड अवक्षेपित कर देती है ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Arrange the following in decreasing order of pKb : Aniline, p-nitroaniline, p-methylaniline
(b) Account for the following : (i) Diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines. (ii) Methylamine in water reacts with FeCl3 to precipitate hydrated ferric oxide.

key_points: (a) Decreasing pKb order: p-nitroaniline > aniline > p-methylaniline
(b)(i) In aromatic diazonium salts, the positive charge on nitrogen is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring; aliphatic diazonium ions lack this resonance stabilisation.
(b)(ii) Methylamine is basic; it generates OH- in water, which precipitates Fe(OH)3 (hydrated ferric oxide) from FeCl3 solution.

questions.solution:
(a) A higher pKb means a weaker base (lower basicity). p-Nitroaniline is the weakest base because the -NO2 group is electron-withdrawing (by both -I and -M effects), reducing electron density on the nitrogen and making it less able to donate a lone pair; it has the highest pKb. Aniline has intermediate pKb. p-Methylaniline is the strongest base among the three because the -CH3 group is electron-donating (+I effect), increasing electron density on nitrogen; it has the lowest pKb. Decreasing pKb order: p-nitroaniline > aniline > p-methylaniline.

(b)(i) In aromatic diazonium salts (ArN2+), the positive charge on the diazonium nitrogen is delocalised over the benzene ring through resonance, which stabilises the ion. Aliphatic diazonium ions (RN2+) have no such resonance stabilisation and are highly unstable, decomposing immediately with loss of N2.

(ii) Methylamine (CH3NH2) is a stronger base than water. In aqueous solution it produces OH- ions: CH3NH2 + H2O ⇌ CH3NH3+ + OH-. These OH- ions react with Fe3+ from FeCl3 to form insoluble Fe(OH)3 (hydrated ferric oxide): Fe3+ + 3OH- → Fe(OH)3↓.

(a) 4-chloroethylbenzene + Br2, Heat → ?

OR
(B) How do you convert :
(a) Chlorobenzene to biphenyl
(b) Propene to 1-Iodopropane
(c) 2-bromobutane to but-2-ene.

key_points: (A)(a) Free radical bromination at benzylic position: product is 4-ClC6H4-CHBr-CH3
(A)(b) Markovnikov addition: HBr adds across double bond; product is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane
(A)(c) The -OH group at the benzylic position reacts with HCl; the -CH2OH group on C-4 side chain is converted to -CH2Cl; product is 4-(chloromethyl)benzyl alcohol OR both OH groups react
(B)(a) Chlorobenzene → Biphenyl via Ullmann reaction (2 C6H5Cl + Cu, heat → C6H5-C6H5 + CuCl2)
(B)(b) Propene → 1-iodopropane: HI addition anti-Markovnikov via peroxide/radical mechanism, or propene + HBr (peroxide) → 1-bromopropane → 1-iodopropane via Finkelstein reaction
(B)(c) 2-bromobutane → but-2-ene via dehydrohalogenation using alcoholic KOH (E2 elimination)

questions.image_description: The question contains structural formulae: (a) 4-chloroethylbenzene (benzene ring with Cl at para position and CH2-CH3 side chain), (b) 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene (cyclohexene ring with methyl group at C-1), (c) a benzene ring with CH2OH on the ring and HO-H2C- at the 4-position.
questions.solution:
(A)(a) In the presence of Br2 and heat (free radical conditions), halogenation occurs at the benzylic position (the carbon adjacent to the ring) of the ethyl group. The major product is 4-chloro-1-(1-bromoethyl)benzene: 4-ClC6H4-CHBr-CH3.

(A)(b) Addition of HBr to 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene follows Markovnikov's rule: H+ adds to the carbon bearing fewer substituents (C-2), and Br- adds to the more substituted carbon (C-1, which already has the methyl group). The major product is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.

(A)(c) When the benzylic alcohol reacts with HCl under heat, the benzylic -CH2OH is converted to -CH2Cl (SN1 mechanism via stabilised benzylic carbocation). The major product is 4-(chloromethyl)benzyl alcohol (the OH on the ring side chain closer to the activating OH is substituted).

OR

(B)(a) Chlorobenzene is converted to biphenyl by the Ullmann reaction: two moles of chlorobenzene react with copper powder at high temperature (2 C6H5Cl + Cu → C6H5-C6H5 + CuCl2).

(B)(b) Propene is converted to 1-iodopropane in two steps: first, propene reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide (anti-Markovnikov addition) to give 1-bromopropane; then 1-bromopropane is treated with NaI in acetone (Finkelstein reaction) to give 1-iodopropane.

(B)(c) 2-Bromobutane is converted to but-2-ene by dehydrohalogenation: heating with alcoholic KOH gives but-2-ene (major product by Saytzeff's rule) via E2 elimination.

3d संक्रमण श्रेणी के तत्व इस प्रकार दिए गए हैं : Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
निम्नलिखित का उत्तर दीजिए :
(a) कॉपर का E°M2+/M मान असाधारण रूप से धनात्मक है, क्यों ?
(b) कौन सा तत्व +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था में एक प्रबल अपचायक है और क्यों ?
(c) Zn2+ लवण रंगहीन होते हैं, क्यों ?
questions.text_english:
The elements of 3d transition series are given as : Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
Answer the following :
(a) Copper has exceptionally positive E°M2+/M value, why ?
(b) Which element is a strong reducing agent in +2 oxidation state and why ?
(c) Zn2+ salts are colourless. Why ?

key_points: (a) Copper has high enthalpy of atomisation and low hydration enthalpy; the energy released in hydration is insufficient to compensate for the energy needed to remove electrons, resulting in a positive E° value.
(b) Ti (titanium) in +2 oxidation state (Ti2+, configuration 3d2) is a strong reducing agent because Ti2+ → Ti4+ releases two electrons and achieves stability.
(c) Zn2+ has the configuration [Ar]3d10 — fully filled d orbitals. No d-d electronic transitions are possible, so no visible light is absorbed, making Zn2+ salts colourless.

questions.solution:
(a) Copper has an exceptionally high (positive) E°M2+/M value (+0.34 V) compared to other transition metals. This is because copper has a very high enthalpy of atomisation (energy needed to convert solid copper to gaseous atoms) and relatively low hydration enthalpy (energy released when Cu2+ ions are hydrated). The total energy released in the process of Cu2+ formation and hydration is insufficient to overcome the energy required for atomisation and ionisation. Consequently, copper does not readily lose electrons and has a high, positive electrode potential, meaning it is a noble metal.

(b) Among the 3d transition elements, Ti (titanium) in the +2 oxidation state (Ti2+) is a strong reducing agent. Titanium has the configuration [Ar]3d2 in the +2 state and can easily lose two more electrons to attain the +4 state ([Ar]), which represents an empty d-orbital configuration that is stable. This tendency to lose electrons makes Ti2+ a strong reducing agent.

(c) Zn2+ has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d10 — all five d-orbitals are completely filled. For a substance to appear coloured, it must absorb visible light, which in transition metal ions occurs by d-d electronic transitions (an electron moves from a lower-energy to a higher-energy d-orbital). Since all d-orbitals in Zn2+ are completely filled, no such d-d transitions are possible, so no visible light is absorbed and Zn2+ salts appear colourless.

key_points: (a)(i) D-glucose + NH2OH → D-glucose oxime + H2O (aldehyde group reacts to form an oxime, confirming aldehyde/carbonyl nature of glucose)
(a)(ii) D-glucose + 5(CH3CO)2O → D-glucose pentaacetate + 5CH3COOH (all 5 OH groups are acetylated)
(b) Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is water-soluble. Since it is not stored in adipose tissue (fat), excess vitamin C is readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored in the body.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) D-glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (NH2OH) to form D-glucose oxime and water:
D-glucose (CHO group) + NH2OH → D-glucose oxime (CH=N-OH) + H2O.
This reaction confirms the presence of an aldehyde group in glucose.

(a)(ii) D-glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate, since all five hydroxyl groups in glucose are acetylated:
D-glucose + 5(CH3CO)2O → D-glucose pentaacetate + 5CH3COOH.
This reaction confirms the presence of five free hydroxyl groups in glucose.

(b) Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble vitamin. Water-soluble vitamins cannot be stored in the body because they dissolve in water and any excess amount is readily filtered out by the kidneys and excreted in urine. Unlike fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), which are stored in adipose (fatty) tissue and the liver, vitamin C has no reservoir in the body, so it must be supplied regularly in the diet.

Since, the OH group increases the electron density more to o- and p- positions therefore OH group is ortho, para-directing. sub_questions.text: क्या होता है जब फ़ीनॉल निम्न से अभिक्रिया करता है ? (i) Br2/CS2 (ii) सांद्र HNO3

key_points: (i) Br2 in CS2 (non-polar solvent, no Lewis acid needed): monobromination at ortho or para position; major product is o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol (low temperature, dilute conditions)
(ii) Conc. HNO3: nitration at ortho and para positions; mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol; with excess conc. HNO3/H2SO4 gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) When phenol reacts with Br2 dissolved in CS2 (carbon disulphide, a non-polar solvent, mild conditions), electrophilic bromination occurs. The OH group activates the ring at ortho and para positions, so the product is a mixture of o-bromophenol (2-bromophenol) and p-bromophenol (4-bromophenol). Because the reaction is in a non-polar solvent without a Lewis acid catalyst, only one bromine is introduced.

(ii) When phenol reacts with concentrated nitric acid (conc. HNO3) alone (without H2SO4), electrophilic nitration gives a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol. When phenol is treated with a mixture of conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4, further nitration produces 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid), a yellow explosive compound.

sub_questions.text_english: Why phenol does not undergo protonation readily ?

key_points: The lone pair on the oxygen atom of phenol is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, reducing the electron density on oxygen and making it less basic, so phenol does not readily accept a proton.

sub_questions.solution: Phenol does not undergo protonation readily because the lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance. This conjugation reduces the electron density on the oxygen, making it a much weaker base (pKb very high) and hence less able to accept a proton (H+). The resonance stabilisation of the phenoxide ion after deprotonation also makes phenol more acidic than basic.

Which is a stronger acid — phenol or cresol ? Give reason.
OR
Write the IUPAC name of the product formed in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

key_points: Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol. Cresol has an electron-donating methyl group (-CH3) that increases electron density on the ring and on the O-H oxygen, destabilising the phenoxide ion and reducing acidity.
OR: The product of the Reimer-Tiemann reaction is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde); IUPAC name: 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

sub_questions.solution:
Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol. Cresol (methylphenol) has a methyl group (-CH3) attached to the benzene ring. The methyl group is an electron-donating group (through +I and hyperconjugation effects), which increases the electron density on the ring and on the oxygen atom. This destabilises the cresoxide ion (the conjugate base) relative to phenoxide ion, making it harder for cresol to lose a proton. Therefore, cresol is less acidic (weaker acid) than phenol.

OR

In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with chloroform (CHCl3) and sodium hydroxide to introduce an aldehyde group at the ortho position of the benzene ring. The product is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, also known as salicylaldehyde. Its IUPAC name is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

questions.text_english: The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed either in terms of decrease in the concentration of reactants or increase in the concentration of a product per unit time. Rate of the reaction depends upon the nature of reactants, concentration of reactants, temperature, presence of catalyst, surface area of the reactants and presence of light. Rate of reaction is directly related to the concentration of reactant. Rate law states that the rate of reaction depends upon the concentration terms on which the rate of reaction actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentration of the reactants in the Rate law expression is called order of reaction while the number of reacting species taking part in an elementary reaction which must collide simultaneously in order to bring about a chemical reaction is called molecularity of the reaction.

sub_questions.text: (i) वेग निर्धारक पद क्या है ? (ii) जटिल अभिक्रिया को परिभाषित कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) What is a rate determining step ? (ii) Define complex reaction.

key_points: Rate determining step: the slowest step in a multi-step reaction mechanism that determines the overall rate of the reaction.
Complex reaction: a reaction that takes place in two or more steps (elementary steps); it proceeds through an intermediate and cannot occur in a single collision.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The rate determining step is the slowest step in the mechanism of a multi-step (complex) reaction. Since it is the slowest, it controls the overall rate at which the reaction proceeds, just as the slowest link in a chain determines the overall speed. The rate law for the overall reaction is determined by the rate law of this slowest step.

(ii) A complex reaction (also called a multi-step reaction) is one that does not occur in a single elementary step but proceeds through a sequence of two or more elementary steps involving one or more intermediate species. The overall chemical equation is the sum of all the elementary steps.

sub_questions.text: वेग स्थिरांक पर ताप का क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the effect of temperature on the rate constant of a reaction ?

key_points: The rate constant increases with increase in temperature. Generally, for every 10°C rise in temperature, the rate constant approximately doubles (temperature coefficient ≈ 2). This is quantified by the Arrhenius equation: k = A·e^(-Ea/RT).

sub_questions.solution: The rate constant (k) of a reaction increases with an increase in temperature. According to the Arrhenius equation k = A × e^(−Ea/RT), as temperature (T) increases, the exponential term e^(−Ea/RT) increases, leading to a higher value of k. Approximately, for every 10 K rise in temperature the rate constant doubles (temperature coefficient = 2). This happens because more molecules acquire energy equal to or greater than the activation energy (Ea) at higher temperatures.

sub_questions.text: आण्विकता केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए ही क्यों लागू होती है जबकि कोटि प्राथमिक और जटिल अभिक्रिया दोनों के लिए लागू होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is molecularity applicable only for elementary reactions whereas order is applicable for elementary as well as complex reactions ?

key_points: Molecularity is the number of molecules colliding simultaneously in a single elementary step, so it is defined only for elementary reactions. For complex reactions, each step has its own molecularity, and the concept does not apply to the overall reaction.
Order is an experimental quantity determined from the rate law; it can be fractional, zero, or integer, and is determined experimentally for both elementary and complex reactions.

sub_questions.solution: Molecularity is a theoretical concept defined as the number of reacting species (atoms, ions, or molecules) that must collide simultaneously in a single elementary step. For a complex reaction, the reaction proceeds through multiple elementary steps, each with its own molecularity; there is no single collision event for the overall reaction, so molecularity of a complex reaction is meaningless. Order, on the other hand, is determined experimentally from the rate law expression (rate = k[A]^m[B]^n). It is the sum of powers of concentration terms and can be zero, fractional, or integer. It applies to any reaction — elementary or complex — because it is derived from experimental data about the actual rate.

sub_questions.text: अणु X का Y में रूपांतरण द्वितीय कोटि की बलगतिकी के अनुरूप होता है । यदि X की सांद्रता तीन गुनी कर दी जाए तो Y के निर्माण होने के वेग पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा ?
sub_questions.text_english: The conversion of molecule X to Y follows second order kinetics. If concentration of X is increased 3 times, how will it affect the rate of formation of Y ?

key_points: For a second order reaction, rate = k[X]^2. If [X] becomes 3[X], new rate = k(3[X])^2 = 9k[X]^2. The rate increases 9 times.

sub_questions.solution: The conversion of X to Y follows second order kinetics, so the rate law is: Rate = k[X]^2. If the concentration of X is tripled (becomes 3[X]), the new rate becomes: New rate = k(3[X])^2 = 9k[X]^2 = 9 × original rate. Therefore, the rate of formation of Y will increase by 9 times when the concentration of X is tripled.

questions.text_english:
(A) (a) Carry out the following conversions : (i) Ethanal to But-2-enal (ii) Propanoic acid to ethane
(b) An alkene A with molecular formula C5H10 on ozonolysis gives a mixture of two compounds B and C. Compound B gives positive Fehling test and also reacts with iodine and NaOH solution. Compound C does not give Fehling solution test but forms iodoform. Identify the compounds A, B and C.
OR
(B) An organic compound (A) (molecular formula C8H16O2) was hydrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid to get a carboxylic acid (B) and an alcohol (C). Oxidation of (C) with chromic acid produced (B). (C) on dehydration gives But-1-ene. Identify (A), (B) and (C) and write chemical equations for the reactions involved.

key_points: (A)(a)(i) Ethanal to but-2-enal: Aldol condensation of ethanal gives 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol), followed by dehydration (acid/heat) to give but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde): CH3CHO + CH3CHO → CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO → CH3CH=CHCHO
(A)(a)(ii) Propanoic acid to ethane: Propanoic acid undergoes decarboxylation with NaOH and CaO (soda lime): CH3CH2COONa + NaOH → CH3CH3 + Na2CO3 (actually gives ethane)
(A)(b) A = CH3CH=C(CH3)2 (2-methylbut-2-ene); B = CH3CHO (ethanal, gives positive Fehling and iodoform); C = CH3COCH3 (propanone/acetone, does not give Fehling but gives iodoform)
(B) C = butan-1-ol (since dehydration gives but-1-ene); B = butanoic acid (C3H7COOH, since oxidation of C4 alcohol gives C4 acid and acid from hydrolysis of ester); A = butyl butanoate (C3H7COOC4H9)

questions.solution:
(A)(a)(i) Ethanal to But-2-enal (Crotonaldehyde):
Step 1 — Aldol condensation: Two molecules of ethanal (CH3CHO) react in the presence of dilute NaOH to give 3-hydroxybutanal (acetaldol): CH3CHO + CH3CHO →(dil. NaOH)→ CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO.
Step 2 — Dehydration: On heating 3-hydroxybutanal with acid or base, water is eliminated to give but-2-enal: CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO →(heat, -H2O)→ CH3CH=CHCHO (but-2-enal).

(A)(a)(ii) Propanoic acid to Ethane:
Propanoic acid is converted to its sodium salt (sodium propanoate) by treating with NaOH. On heating sodium propanoate with sodalime (NaOH + CaO), decarboxylation occurs: CH3CH2COONa + NaOH →(CaO, heat)→ CH3CH3 (ethane) + Na2CO3.

(A)(b) Molecular formula of A is C5H10 (an alkene). Ozonolysis gives B and C.
B gives a positive Fehling test → B is an aldehyde. B also reacts with I2/NaOH (iodoform test) → B is ethanal (CH3CHO), since only ethanal among common aldehydes gives iodoform.
C does not give Fehling test (not an aldehyde) but gives iodoform → C is a methyl ketone. With molecular formula considerations, C is propanone (CH3COCH3).
Since B = CH3CHO (2C) and C = CH3COCH3 (3C), total carbons in A = 2 + 3 = 5. A is therefore 2-methylbut-2-ene: CH3-C(CH3)=CH-CH3. Ozonolysis of CH3-C(CH3)=CH-CH3 gives CH3COCH3 (from the C(CH3) side) and CH3CHO (from the CH-CH3 side).

OR

(B) Compound A (C8H16O2) is an ester (hydrolysis gives acid B + alcohol C).
C on dehydration gives but-1-ene → C is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH), a primary alcohol.
Oxidation of C with chromic acid gives B → B is butanoic acid (CH3CH2CH2COOH).
Since B = butanoic acid (C4H8O2) and C = butan-1-ol (C4H10O), A = butyl butanoate (CH3CH2CH2COOCH2CH2CH2CH3, molecular formula C8H16O2).

Chemical equations:
(1) Hydrolysis: CH3CH2CH2COOC4H9 + H2O →(dil. H2SO4)→ CH3CH2CH2COOH + C4H9OH
(2) Oxidation: CH3CH2CH2CH2OH + [O] →(CrO3/H+)→ CH3CH2CH2COOH
(3) Dehydration: CH3CH2CH2CH2OH →(conc. H2SO4, 170°C)→ CH2=CHCH2CH3 (but-1-ene) + H2O

(A) For the complex [Fe(en)2Cl2]Cl, identify :
(a) the oxidation number of iron.
(b) the hybridization and the shape of the complex.
(c) the magnetic behaviour of the complex
(d) whether there is an optical isomer of the complex ? If so draw its structure.
(e) IUPAC name of the complex.
(At. no. of Fe = 26)
OR
(B) (a) Using IUPAC norms write the names of the following :
(i) [Co(NH3)4Cl(NO2)]Cl (ii) K3[Fe(CN)6] (iii) [Cr(C2O4)3]3-
(b) What is crystal field splitting energy ? Why low spin tetrahedral complexes are not formed ?

key_points: (A)(a) Oxidation state of Fe: en is neutral, Cl- is -1 each (2 Cl in coordination sphere + 1 outside); total charge on complex cation = +1 (one Cl- outside). So x + 0×2 + (-1)×2 = +1; x = +3.
(A)(b) Fe3+ has configuration [Ar]3d5; with en (strong field) and Cl- (weak field) — d2sp3 hybridisation (inner orbital); octahedral shape.
(A)(c) Fe3+ in 3d5 — with mixed ligands (en strong, Cl- weak) — complex is likely high spin, paramagnetic (unpaired electrons present).
(A)(d) [Fe(en)2Cl2]+ is a cis-trans isomer. The cis isomer has optical isomers (non-superimposable mirror images — Δ and Λ forms). Trans isomer does not.
(A)(e) IUPAC: dichlorido bis(ethane-1,2-diamine)iron(III) chloride
(B)(a)(i) Tetraamminechloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride; (ii) Potassium hexacyanoferrate(III); (iii) Tris(oxalato)chromate(III) ion

(B)(b) Crystal field splitting energy (Δ) is the energy difference between the two sets of d-orbitals (eg and t2g) in an octahedral field. In tetrahedral complexes, Δt ≈ 4/9 Δo (much smaller), so the pairing energy always exceeds Δt and electrons remain unpaired (high spin); low spin tetrahedral complexes are not formed.

questions.solution:
(A)(a) In [Fe(en)2Cl2]Cl, ethylenediamine (en) is a neutral bidentate ligand and Cl- carries -1 charge. The complex ion is [Fe(en)2Cl2]+ (one Cl- is the counter ion outside). Let Fe oxidation state = x: x + 2(0) + 2(-1) = +1, so x = +3. Iron is in the +3 oxidation state.

(A)(b) Fe (Z=26) configuration: [Ar]3d6 4s2. Fe3+: [Ar]3d5. Ethylenediamine is a strong field ligand; 2 Cl- are weak field ligands. In [Fe(en)2Cl2]+, Fe3+ undergoes d2sp3 hybridisation (using two 3d, one 4s, and three 4p orbitals). The geometry is octahedral.

(A)(c) In Fe3+ with d5 configuration, even with strong field ligands, having both strong (en) and weak (Cl-) field ligands makes this a weak/intermediate field complex. Fe3+ d5 — 5 unpaired electrons (high spin). The complex is paramagnetic.

(A)(d) The complex [Fe(en)2Cl2]+ can exist as cis and trans geometric isomers. The cis isomer (both Cl- on the same side) is chiral and exists as two non-superimposable mirror images — the Δ (delta, right-handed propeller) and Λ (lambda, left-handed propeller) optical isomers. The trans isomer (Cl- on opposite sides) is achiral. So yes, the complex has optical isomers (only the cis form).

(A)(e) IUPAC name: Dichloridebis(ethane-1,2-diamine)iron(III) chloride.

OR

(B)(a)(i) In [Co(NH3)4Cl(NO2)]Cl: Co is the metal; NH3 = ammine (×4), Cl- = chlorido, NO2- = nitrito-N (bonded through N). Co oxidation state: x + 0(4) + (-1) + (-1) = +1 (one Cl- outside), so x = +3. IUPAC name: Tetraamminechloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride.

(ii) K3[Fe(CN)6]: three K+ outside; [Fe(CN)6]3- is the complex anion; CN- = cyano (×6); Fe: x + 6(-1) = -3, x = +3. Name: Potassium hexacyanoferrate(III).

(iii) [Cr(C2O4)3]3-: C2O4^2- = oxalato (×3); Cr: x + 3(-2) = -3, x = +3. Name: Tris(oxalato)chromate(III) ion.

(B)(b) Crystal field splitting energy (Δo or CFSE) is the energy difference between the higher energy eg set (dx2-y2 and dz2) and the lower energy t2g set (dxy, dyz, dxz) of d-orbitals when a central metal ion is surrounded by ligands in an octahedral field. The ligands act as point charges and destabilise the eg orbitals more than t2g, creating an energy gap Δo.

Low spin tetrahedral complexes are not formed because the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral field (Δt) is only about 4/9 of the octahedral splitting (Δo): Δt ≈ (4/9)Δo. This smaller splitting means the pairing energy (energy needed to force two electrons into the same orbital) almost always exceeds Δt. Electrons therefore remain unpaired to minimise energy, always resulting in high spin configuration. Since low spin requires the splitting energy to overcome pairing energy, and Δt is too small to do this, low spin tetrahedral complexes are not observed.

questions.text_english:
(A) (a) Write the cell reaction and calculate the e.m.f. of the following cell at 298 K :
Sn(s) | Sn2+ (0.004 M) || H+ (0.02 M) | H2(g) (1 Bar) | Pt(s)
(Given : E°Sn2+/Sn = −0.14 V, E°H+|H2(g),Pt = 0.00 V)
(b) Account for the following :
(i) On the basis of E° values, O2 gas should be liberated at anode but it is Cl2 gas which is liberated in the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl.
(ii) Conductivity of CH3COOH decreases on dilution.
OR
(B) (a) Write the anode and cathode reactions and the overall cell reaction occurring in a lead storage battery during its use.
(b) Calculate the potential for half-cell containing 0.01 M K2Cr2O7(aq), 0.01 M Cr3+(aq) and 1.0 × 10−4 M H+(aq).
The half cell reaction is Cr2O7^2-(aq) + 14H+(aq) + 6e- → 2Cr3+(aq) + 7H2O(l)
and the standard electrode potential is given as E° = 1.33 V.
[Given : log 10 = 1]

key_points: (A)(b)(i) Overpotential: although E° favours O2, the actual (overpotential-corrected) potential for Cl2 evolution is lower in practice due to overvoltage effects; Cl- is present in high concentration and its discharge is kinetically favoured.

(A)(b)(ii) CH3COOH is a weak acid; on dilution, degree of dissociation increases but the number of ions per unit volume decreases. The molar conductivity increases but conductivity (K) = molar conductivity × concentration decreases.
(B)(a) Anode: Pb + SO4^2- → PbSO4 + 2e-; Cathode: PbO2 + 4H+ + SO4^2- + 2e- → PbSO4 + 2H2O; Overall: Pb + PbO2 + 4H+ + 2SO4^2- → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O

questions.solution:
(A)(a) Cell reaction: Sn(s) + 2H+(aq) → Sn2+(aq) + H2(g) [Sn is oxidised at anode; H+ is reduced at cathode].
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.00 − (−0.14) = +0.14 V.
Using Nernst equation (n = 2):
E = E°cell − (0.0591/2) × log([Sn2+] × P(H2) / [H+]2)
= 0.14 − (0.02955) × log(0.004 × 1 / (0.02)2)
= 0.14 − 0.02955 × log(0.004 / 0.0004)
= 0.14 − 0.02955 × log(10)
= 0.14 − 0.02955 × 1
= 0.14 − 0.02955 ≈ 0.1104 V ≈ 0.11 V.

(A)(b)(i) According to standard electrode potential values, the E° for O2 evolution (1.23 V) is lower than that for Cl2 evolution (1.36 V), which suggests O2 should be liberated preferentially. However, in practice, Cl2 is liberated during electrolysis of aqueous NaCl because of the phenomenon of overpotential (overvoltage). The O2 electrode has a very high overpotential (extra energy needed to initiate the reaction), which raises its actual liberation potential above that of Cl2. Additionally, in concentrated NaCl solution, the high concentration of Cl- ions near the electrode makes Cl2 evolution kinetically favoured.

(A)(b)(ii) Conductivity (κ) of a solution = Molar conductivity (Λm) × Concentration (C). For CH3COOH, a weak acid, on dilution the degree of dissociation (α) increases, producing more ions, so Λm increases. However, the concentration C decreases much more steeply. Since κ = Λm × C and C decreases faster than Λm increases, the overall conductivity κ decreases on dilution.

OR

(B)(a) In a lead storage battery during discharge:
Anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO4^2-(aq) → PbSO4(s) + 2e-
Cathode (reduction): PbO2(s) + 4H+(aq) + SO4^2-(aq) + 2e- → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l)
Overall cell reaction: Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) → 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l)

(B)(b) Half-cell reaction: Cr2O7^2-(aq) + 14H+(aq) + 6e- → 2Cr3+(aq) + 7H2O(l); E° = 1.33 V, n = 6.
[Cr2O7^2-] = 0.01 M (from 0.01 M K2Cr2O7, fully dissociated); [Cr3+] = 0.01 M; [H+] = 1.0 × 10−4 M.

Reaction quotient Q = [Cr3+]2 / ([Cr2O7^2-][H+]^14)
= (0.01)2 / (0.01 × (10-4)^14)
= 10^-4 / (10^-2 × 10^-56)
= 10^-4 / 10^-58 = 10^54.

log Q = 54.

Using Nernst equation:
E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log Q
= 1.33 − (0.0591/6) × 54
= 1.33 − 0.00985 × 54
= 1.33 − 0.5319
≈ 0.7981 V ≈ 0.80 V.
